newsitem.title: USA: Sanmina to buy Comptronix assets.
newsitem.headline: Sanmina to buy Comptronix assets.

text.p: Comptronix Corp said on Friday it agreed to sell substantially all its assets to Sanmina Corp for $20 million to $22 million in cash.
Comptronix, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in August, said in a statement it had signed a definitive agreement with Sanmina.
"The estimated purchase price range for the assets, which is based on a formula in the definitive agreement, is $20 million to $22 million, payable in cash," it said.

Consummation of the acquisition depends on several conditions, including the completion of due diligence by Sanmina, the approval of the Bankruptcy Court, and expiration of the applicable waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act.
Comptronix said it expected its secured creditors would be fully repaid and its unsecured creditors would get about $0.10 on the dollar for claims such as unsecured debt and trade payables.
Comptronix provides contract manufacturing services to original equipment manufacturers in the electronics industry.
